newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Schiphol hikes Chapter II restrictions.
newsitem.headline: Schiphol hikes Chapter II restrictions.

text.p: Amsterdam's Schiphol Airport is to beef up the restrictions and charges it imposes on operators of noisy and older Chapter Two aircraft, its operating company said.

The window during which Chapter Two aircraft are forbidden to take off and land will be extended from April 1 from 23:00PM-06:00AM to 18:00PM-8:00. In addition, a range of increased landing fees are being introduced, it stated..
The airport believes the new tougher measures will reduce the number of take-offs and landings by category Two planes from nine pct in 1996 to around five pct this year.
Since November 1995, the airport has adopted a tougher stance on older aircraft types. Ever since it has introduced gradually tougher measures every six months.

Schiphol said that from April 1, Chapter Two aircraft with a maximum payload of 100 tons must pay an extra 1,200 guilders per landing. Operators of aircraft with heavier payloads must be prepared to pay 1,800 guilders per landing, the airport said. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
